title: Umami-active components in edible Fungi: Distribution, structure-function relationships, molecular mechanisms, computational insights and industrial applications.
authors: Khengle, Samruddhi; Kalam, Tejas; Mondal, Imdadul Hoque; Sherin, Zincia; Bashir, Omar; Pawase, Prashant Anil; Kapila, Akshit
one_liner_zh: 该综述探讨食用菌中鲜味化合物的分布、结构与功能关系及工业应用，仅提及CRISPR/Cas9代谢工程作为未来方向，与本课题的CRISPR切割/碱基编辑分子机制无实质关联。
abstract: Edible mushrooms are a biodiverse yet underutilized source of umami compounds providing clean-label alternatives to synthetic flavourings such as monosodium glutamate (MSG). The characteristic savory taste arises from interactions among free amino acids (glutamate, aspartate), 5'-ribonucleotides (5'-GMP, 5'-IMP), organic acids (succinic, citric), polyols (trehalose, mannitol), and bioactive peptides, whose accumulation is influenced by genetic composition, growth substrate, developmental stage, and postharvest management. This review systematically examines the distribution of umami compounds in Pleurotus spp., Lentinula edodes, Hypsizygus marmoreus, and other species, with emphasis on umami peptides, their structure-function relationships, and taste perception mediated by T1R1/T1R3, mGluR1/mGluR4, and CaSR receptors. In addition, it critically assesses industrial applications and advanced computational approaches including iUmami-SCM, UMPred-FRL, Umami-MRNN, Umami-BERT, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations for high-throughput discovery of umami peptides. Enzymatic hydrolysis coupled with ultrafiltration enriches low-molecular-weight (<3 kDa) umami peptides while reducing associated bitterness. Equivalent Umami Concentration (EUC) reflects an 8-10-fold synergistic enhancement between amino acids and nucleotides, where the synergistic constant represents the strength of their non-additive umami interaction. While fungal peptides are highly valued for their unique sensory contributions, their significance extends beyond taste as they also exert multifunctional bioactivities including ACE inhibition (IC(5)(0): 9-150 muM), antioxidant activity (DPPH and ABTS assays), and endothelial protection. Challenges include genetic engineering strategies for umami enhancement, salt-umami interactions, and analytical standards. Emerging industrial applications, including CRISPR/Cas9-based metabolic engineering and agro-waste upcycling, position edible fungi as promising platforms for clean-label flavor systems, sodium reduction, and circular food economies.
abstract_zh: 食用菌是鲜味化合物的一个生物多样性丰富但尚未充分利用的来源，为味精（MSG）等合成调味品提供了清洁标签替代品。其特有的咸鲜味源于游离氨基酸（谷氨酸、天冬氨酸）、5‘-核糖核苷酸（5’-GMP、5‘-IMP）、有机酸（琥珀酸、柠檬酸）、多元醇（海藻糖、甘露醇）和生物活性肽之间的相互作用，这些化合物的积累受遗传组成、生长基质、发育阶段和采后管理的影响。本综述系统考察了侧耳属（Pleurotus spp.）、香菇（Lentinula edodes）、白玉菇（Hypsizygus marmoreus）及其他物种中鲜味化合物的分布，重点探讨鲜味肽、其结构-功能关系以及由T1R1/T1R3、mGluR1/mGluR4和CaSR受体介导的味觉感知。此外，本文还批判性评估了工业应用及先进计算方法，包括iUmami-SCM、UMPred-FRL、Umami-MRNN、Umami-BERT、分子对接和分子动力学模拟，用于鲜味肽的高通量发现。酶解结合超滤可富集低分子量（<3 kDa）鲜味肽，同时降低相关苦味。等效鲜味浓度（EUC）反映氨基酸与核苷酸之间8-10倍的协同增强效应，其中协同常数代表其非加性鲜味相互作用的强度。虽然真菌肽因其独特的感官贡献而备受重视，但其意义超越味觉范畴，因为它们还发挥多功能生物活性，包括ACE抑制（IC(5)(0)：9-150 μM）、抗氧化活性（DPPH和ABTS测定）及内皮保护。挑战包括鲜味增强的基因工程策略、盐-鲜味相互作用及分析标准。新兴工业应用，包括基于CRISPR/Cas9的代谢工程和农业废弃物升级利用，使食用菌成为清洁标签风味系统、减钠和循环食品经济的有前景平台。
